I’ve reviewed the data on buyer demographics, substitute channels, and the two distinct WTP curves for the catalog. The differentiation curve for authentic Japanese formulas (especially JP Curel and SK-II/Shiseido) remains inelastic among Metro Van buyers who value authenticity and DDP pricing, while the arbitrage curve for cheaper alternatives like 7-Eleven or Amazon grey-market is thin and price-sensitive. Curel’s shift to authorized retail at Shoppers is a notable development, but it doesn’t eliminate the trust premium buyers pay for genuine stock.

On elasticity, DDP vs DDU is a clear constraint—40% extra costs and CBSA de minim 20 CAD make DDU conversion a killer. Days-to-door of 7-21 days for consolidated shipments versus 1-3 local is workable, but Narvar’s 73% EDD influence and McKinsey’s 90% wait-time stat suggest buyers expect reliable 24h delivery. Stockout and preorderFit high in the catalog align with weekly consolidation cycles, which buyers already accept from YesStyle.

TAM/SAM/SOM sizing looks reasonable: East Asian VM population ~607k in Metro Van, with 8k-30k potential buyers per year at CAD 50-200 spend. Legal SAM for ex-suns 1-5M CAD is conservative, and Year 1 SOM of 30-45k (base 65-90k) fits within 1-5% capture. Desk 345k GMV ceiling is a merchandising limit, not a demand cap.

The category-by-category table will be the core of the 02-demand-market.md note. I’ll structure it around the three buyer types (Metro Van primary, with HK-born, China, Taiwan, Korea immigrants), listing rules (CA growth ≥12% or index ≥55, JP ≥25, margin ≥28%), and falsifiers by month 6 (preorder conversion < 15-25%, repeat <15-20%, refund >8-10%, CAC > CAD 25-40).
